subject: science
notes: Pumice is a light-colored volcanic rock.
It forms when frothy lava full of gas bubbles cools very quickly during an explosive eruption.
The bubbles leave the hardened rock full of tiny holes, so a piece of pumice is mostly empty space.
Pumice is one of the few rocks that can float on water; after some eruptions, rafts of pumice drift across the sea for months.
stem: The student wants to explain why pumice floats. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Pumice, a light-colored volcanic rock, is one of the few rocks that can float on water.
choices.B: After some volcanic eruptions, rafts of pumice drift across the surface of the sea for months.
choices.C: Pumice forms during explosive volcanic eruptions, when lava cools very quickly into a light-colored rock.
choices.D: Pumice can float because it forms from frothy, gas-filled lava that cools quickly, leaving the rock so full of tiny holes that it is mostly empty space.

explanation.why: To explain why pumice floats, the sentence must connect floating to its cause. The notes give the chain: gas bubbles in the lava leave holes, so the rock is mostly empty space. Only one choice links the floating to that structure.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This states that pumice floats but gives no reason.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This describes what floating pumice does, not why it floats.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This tells how pumice forms but leaves out the gas bubbles and holes, which are what make it float.
explanation.D: Correct. "Because" connects the floating to the holes left by gas bubbles, which is the reason given in the notes.
